Hi Alicja — looping in some quick technical notes so we can use the workshop time efficiently. A few practical items and commands you can try locally before the session:

Auth and local dev
- Fast path: API key stored in environment (REDWOOD_API_KEY) for local dev. Good for quick smoke tests.
- Prod path: OIDC service account + short-lived tokens (we have an OIDC integration guide in the repo).

Routing & model variants
- For low-latency queries use our hosted small-capacity model (cost-optimized). For EU-only and PII workloads route to your Dedicated pool (we’ll provision a trial token).
- Routing example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "X-Redwood-Routing: region=eu;pool=dedicated-trial" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-embedded-small","input":"sumarize product catalog"}'

Embeddings + reranker (small CPU-only flow)
- Embedding step (Python requests): generate embeddings with context window <= 512 tokens; store locally in FAISS.
- Reranker: simple logistic model over feature vector [embedding_cos_sim, bm25_score, recency_offset] — weights in sample model included. The sample pipeline includes a CPU-only PyTorch fallback for reranker.

Structured output / tool calling
- We’ll demo the SDK’s structured-output helpers that validate JSON schema before invoking a local microservice. Sample endpoint call (TS):
  await redwood.callTool('productLookup', { sku: 'ABC123' })

Local smoke tests (in repo root):
- python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
- ./scripts/run_embedding_smoke.sh --sample orchard-data-mapping-sample.csv
- npm install && npm run start:local -> starts TS playground on :3000 (calls local microservice stub)

Repository: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks-playground/tree/orchard-sample (branch contains README with the commands above). We’ll push a small PR that auto-creates the docker-compose for the product-catalog stub so you can run everything without network egress.

I’ve added two small files to the attachments that outline the smoke tests and the CSV mapping sample. We’ll confirm the mutual-TLS constraint if you can share the staging NAT/fqdn details.

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
